messages:
maya: FYI customer in APAC reporting a spike of 502/504s to hosted inference around 11:05 PST. They see a flurry of errors for streaming generation requests, ~40% of calls failing for ~6m. sample x-request-id: 0a1b2c3d. They've already escalated to support with logs.

sam_cs: Customer is enterprise tier, running heavy burst traffic. They're unhappy — want ETA and mitigation. They say retries are doubling token usage and billing spike. 😬

ryan_sre: Can we get a sample request payload + full envoy logs for the time window? Also any recent infra changes in the last 30m? @deploy-bot did anything deploy around 11:00?

maya: Uploading a redacted request and envoy snippet below. Request is a single long streaming call (chunked) with function-calling enabled. x-request-id: 0a1b2c3d-01

maya: ```
POST /v1/generate
Host: api.redwood-inference.prod
Authorization: Bearer <REDACTED>
Content-Type: application/json
X-Request-ID: 0a1b2c3d-01

{ "model": "redwood-large-v2", "stream": true, "inputs": "<large prompt>" }
```

maya: envoy log excerpt: ```
[2026-03-15T11:05:12.345Z] external ~ upstream reset before response":[source/common/http/conn_manager_impl.cc:1234]"
[2026-03-15T11:05:12.346Z] connection error: read reset
```

leila_runtime: I *think* this is Envoy→runtime connection resets when the runtime is busy and we hit HTTP/2 multiplex limits. We recently toggled a change to upstream http2_max_concurrent_streams on the frontdoor pool (to optimize resource usage) — that could cause resets under bursty streaming.

joel_infra: Confirmed: there was an infra config change 10:58 PST that reduced per-upstream concurrent streams from 128 -> 32 for frontdoor->runtime pools. It was intended to reduce memory pressure. change id: cfg-2026-0315-frontend-http2.

ryan_sre: That matches. When streams hit the limit Envoy can reset inflight streams which shows as 502/504 to the client. We should revert the cfg asap or bump limits for this pool.

alice_billing: Customer reported token usage doubled due to automatic client retries. We should consider waiving overage or retro credit while we fix. I'll prepare a note but need confirmation of affected window.

oncall: I can roll back the change now. Quick mitigation options:
- revert cfg-2026-0315-frontend-http2 (fast rollback)
- increase upstream timeout and connection keepalive settings
- add a temporary per-route retry with 1 retry and 1s backoff to smooth client retries

deploy-bot: canary-deploy cfg-2026-0315-frontend-http2 applied to 15% of frontdoor nodes at 10:59 PST (canary finished at 11:03 PST).

maya: Repro steps from customer (they provided):
1) Hit streaming endpoint with 50 concurrent streams from a single connection using http/2 multiplexing.
2) Payloads ~16k tokens each.
3) Observe intermittent 502/504 after ~30s.

maya: curl repro (sanitized):
```bash
for i in {1..50}; do \
  curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer <TOKEN>" -H "X-Request-ID: test-$i" \
  -d '{"model":"redwood-large-v2","stream":true,"inputs":"<big>"}' \
  https://api.redwood-inference.prod/v1/generate &\
done
wait
```

leila_runtime: Additional logs from runtime show: `kv-cache miss` spikes right before resets, and worker thread pool saturates. The combination of high per-connection multiplexing + longer token generation increases concurrency inside the runtime beyond safe limits.

ryan_sre: Plan: immediate rollback of cfg-2026-0315-frontend-http2 (rollback approved), then adjust http2_max_concurrent_streams to 96 (instead of 128) and increase upstream idle timeout to 90s. We'll monitor errors for 30m.

joel_infra: Rolling back now on frontdoor fleet. Command run: ```bash
infractl config rollback cfg-2026-0315-frontend-http2 --target frontdoor --force
```
rolling to 100% with graceful drain.

deploy-bot: rollback job started at 11:12 PST, target: frontdoor (all nodes).

maya: Customer confirmed error rate dropping within 3m of rollback; still watching. :relieved:

alice_billing: I'll put a temporary credit hold and open a billing ticket. Recommend 1) credit for retry-induced tokens between 11:00-11:12 PST, 2) follow-up after monitoring.

ryan_sre: Postmortem actions / follow-ups:
- revert change and set better canary criteria for frontdoor http2 tuning (ryan_sre)
- add telemetry to detect upstream reset spikes and auto-alert (leila_runtime)
- run a controlled load test for streaming http/2 multiplexing cases (eng-sre + runtime)
- billing credit for impacted customers (alice_billing)

oncall: Marking incident as mitigated at 11:15 PST; will keep channel open for 2h for regression.

sam_cs: Communicated mitigation to customer, will follow up on credits and timeline.

maya: Thanks team — closing thread after monitoring window.
